name: Jehoahaz
overview: Jehoahaz was a male king of Judah and the son of Josiah. His reign is marked by doing evil in the sight of the LORD, indicating a failure to follow God's commands during his leadership. This characterization situates him within the biblical narrative as a ruler who did not uphold the covenantal standards expected of Judah's kings.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehoahaz means 'YHWH holds,' reflecting a connection to the LORD, though it was not given directly by God. He is also known by several other names such as Johanan, meaning 'YHWH is gracious,' Joahaz, with the same meaning as Jehoahaz, and Shallum, meaning 'peace, well-being, prosperity.' Additionally, he held the title King of Judah, emphasizing his royal status.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jehoahaz as the son of Josiah. It is also inferred that his mother was Hamutal. Beyond these relationships, the biblical text does not provide further family details for Jehoahaz.
scriptureSignificance: Jehoahaz's significance lies in his role as a successor to Josiah and king of Judah who failed to maintain faithfulness to the LORD. His evil actions contributed to the spiritual decline of Judah, contrasting with his father's reforms. This highlights the ongoing struggle within Judah's monarchy between faithfulness and disobedience to God.
